description.narrative: The GFP is a catalytic mechanism, designed to unlock and channel private and blended capital for green development projects by strengthening sustainable finance ecosystems, developing bankable project pipelines, and improving access to financing for SMEs. Through targeted tools - such as green bonds, carbon pricing, debt-for-nature swaps, and tax incentives - anchored in national frameworks like Integrated National Financing Frameworks (INFFs) and NDCs, GFP translates policy into tangible investments, aiming to catalyze at least USD 240 million in private capital by 2029. Operating through a dual-track approach that strengthens ecosystems while activating transactions, GFP connects policy and market realities by strengthening foundational systems while mobilizing green finance at scale. It tailors for a country-driven approach within a shared regional framework which prioritizes systemic transformation. By engaging ministries, financial institutions, and global partners, GFP translates climate ambitions into investable opportunities, fosters regional cooperation, and equips countries with the tools and partnerships needed to drive a just, green transition. The GFP’s overall objective is to unlock and mobilize private green finance and strengthen sustainable private investment ecosystems to accelerate inclusive green growth in the Arab States, achieved through two interconnected outcomes: (1) enabling environments and green investment pipelines strengthened, and (2) private capital mobilized and green investment pipelines expanded.
